title: Trump Tightens Iran Deal Terms Further; Tells CBS News He Is 'In No Hurry' to Close a Deal
detail: President Trump further tightened the terms of the proposed US-Iran peace deal on May 31, 2026 — Day 92 of the US-Iran war — with no final agreement signed. US officials said Tehran may take several days to respond to Trump's new and more demanding terms. Trump told CBS News he is 'in no hurry' to finalize an Iran deal, signaling he retains leverage and is not under domestic pressure to close an agreement quickly. Al Jazeera reported Trump had tightened terms beyond the May 30 framework, which itself had already escalated demands to include destruction of Iran's 440.9 kg highly enriched uranium stockpile. The Strait of Hormuz remains partially blockaded with US naval forces maintaining their presence. Oil markets remain volatile above $100/bbl as the uncertainty continues. Iranian officials are reviewing the new terms — diplomats described the situation as 'talks about talks' as the substantive gaps remain wide.

media.caption: Trump further tightens Iran deal terms on Day 92; tells CBS he is 'in no hurry' as Iran reviews new demands

title: Trump Approval Hits New Low in Multiple Polls — Silver Bulletin Net -19.1; YouGov/Economist 34%; Record -47 Net on Inflation
detail: Multiple polls released around May 29-31, 2026 showed Trump's approval ratings at or near record lows for either presidential term. The Silver Bulletin aggregate (Nate Silver) showed net approval at -19.1 — the lowest aggregate reading of either Trump term. The Economist/YouGov poll recorded 34% approval / 59% disapproval — the lowest in that tracking series. Emerson College showed 39% approval. Trump's net approval on handling inflation hit a historic low of -47, with only 24-25% of Americans approving of his economic performance. Democrats led the generic congressional ballot by +8 points, though Republicans' structural redistricting advantage of approximately 10 House seats may prevent Democrats from recapturing the House majority. Trump's support among white Americans without college degrees has fallen to 49% — down from 63% in February 2025 — and among Republicans broadly to 68% (from 73% in January 2025).

media.caption: Trump approval rating hits new lows: Silver Bulletin net -19.1, YouGov/Economist 34%, inflation approval net -47
